headline: As chip industry chases AI, U.S. national labs look to newcomers for supercomputers
summary: In a nondescript building on Kirtland Air Force Base on the high desert of New Mexico, liquid-cooled supercomputers gurgle and hum their way through some of the most complex math problems the U.S. government seeks to solve: simulating how hypersonic nuclear weapons would ‌move through the earth's atmosphere, or what would happen if one nuclear warhead detonated near another.  For more than a decade, the chips handling this secretive and demanding work ‌came from mainstream semiconductor firms like Nvidia or Advanced Micro Devices.  But with those companies increasingly designing their chips for artificial intelligence and facing supply shortages, the managers in charge of the systems at Sandia National Laboratories, which operates ​the machines at Kirtland and is one of three U.S. labs tasked with developing and maintaining the nation's nuclear weapons arsenal, are increasingly unsure how they will find computing power for high-precision scientific work like theirs.

And it includes all the data centers, CPUs. This is a new market for us."Lenovo reported a better-than-expected 27% jump in quarterly revenueThe tech firm's tablet and smartphone division saw revenue rise by close to a quarter - it's highest growth rate in five years.Lenovo said overall revenue for the period to the end of March jumped $21.6 billion - above analyst estimates.Investors liked what they heard and shares soared 15% soon after the update.Texas sued WhatsApp and its parent firm Meta.The state said the tech firm misled consumers over the messaging app’s encryption and privacy standards.The lawsuit says users are given false assurance that their messages are encrypted.A Meta spokesman called the allegations “false”, and said WhatsApp can't access people’s encrypted messages.Samsung shares surged after it reached a deal with its South Korean union to avoid an 18-day strike.48,000 workers could have taken part in the proposed industrial action.One union source said a memory chip worker with a base salary of about $53,000 is expected to receive a bonus of around $416,000.There was relief in Seoul at the deal as Samsung makes up for about a quarter of the country's exports.Although the Samsung Electronics Co Union, which has about 13,000 members, took legal action to stop the vote on a pay deal - which is expected to be concluded by Wednesday.It said it took legal action after being told it had no right to join the vote.
